reason: This book's problem has been churn, not thesis: eight legs in nine weeks for -3.20% while SPY is +2.73%, and a cross-sectional sector-momentum book that is re-ranked every week never gives the ranking time to pay. The current leg is two sessions old and the macro it was ranked for was confirmed this week rather than falsified: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% with a hawkish dot plot and ~90% odds of a December hike, the 10-year touched 5.00% and the curve flattened hard, Brent held above $100, and the rate-sensitive short side of the book (industrials, transports, discretionary, small caps) has now fallen five consecutive weeks according to Friday's market review, with the Dow -1.7% on the week and the Russell -0.5% on Friday. The leg's marks are a wash so far (longs XBI +1.65%, XLE +0.44%, XLV +0.37%, XLF -0.13%, XLC -1.94%; shorts XLU +0.53%, XHB +0.42%, XLI -0.62%, XLY -0.77%), and the two legs going against me are small and stop-protected: XLC's drop is a single-name Netflix downgrade on a Wells Fargo viewership call inside a 7% sleeve with a -12% stop, and XLY's +1.4% Friday bounce came on iPhone 18 launch day inside a 5% short with a -12% stop. I looked hardest at the XLU short, because utilities are being bid as an AI-power and defensive rotation play, but with the 10-year at 5% a 3% dividend sector is the wrong duration to own into further hikes, the mark is still in my favour, and the -10% stop bounds the squeeze risk. Every leg carries a hard stop and take-profit, so the engine already does the risk management a re-rank would do, and a full nine-leg replacement would cost roughly 35-40bps round trip plus fresh borrow on the shorts to land on a near-identical ranking. Next week's PCE, GDP and Micron print are exactly the catalysts this ranking was built to express (sticky inflation, hiking Fed, energy and health care over rate-sensitive cyclicals), so I let the leg run at least through them. Same-direction overlap with my Round 2 book is only XLE long (8% of 66% gross), well inside the novelty rule.
